stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Mesloub to replace Gabriel at Man United?
stories.summary: Could Lens winger Mezian Mesloub be Manchester United's latest teenage signing? Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Manchester United have lined up 16-year-old Lens winger Mezian Mesloub to replace JJ Gabriel, while Borussia Dortmund forward Maximilian Beier is on the radar of Arsenal. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United have lined up Lens winger Mezian Mesloub as a potential long-term target, TEAMtalk reports. Scouts from United, Arsenal, Chelsea, Paris Saint-Germain, and Monaco have tracked the 16-year-old, while Red Devils executives Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox continue efforts to convince JJ Gabriel to stay.

- Arsenal are monitoring Borussia Dortmund forward Maximilian Beier as a potential attacking reinforcement, TEAMtalk has revealed. Gunners scouts have been impressed by the 23-year-old's versatility across the frontline during their visits to monitor Ethan Nwaneri's loan spell at the German club.

- Real Madrid are assessing a move for Manchester United youngster Gabriel, according to Diario AS. Sources have told ESPN that the 15-year-old has indicated his desire to leave Old Trafford, prompting contact from Real Madrid while they evaluate eligibility requirements, with Barcelona and Bayern Munich also competing for his signature.

- Tottenham Hotspur could renew their pursuit of Nottingham Forest midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White in January, according to Football Insider. Spurs remain interested in the 26-year-old after attempting to sign him in the summer of 2025, with potential reinforcements being assessed following a difficult start to the season, but could face paying a fee of £125 million. By contrast, the England international has started the campaign strongly, registering three goal involvements in five Premier League outings.

- Atlético Madrid are set to revive their pursuit of Bayer Leverkusen midfielder Ibrahim Maza, according to Goal. The 20-year-old Algeria international's transfer could command a fee of around €70 million, though Leverkusen remain determined to retain him and are working on a contract extension with a pay rise.

Other rumors
- Liverpool could revive their interest in Brighton & Hove Albion winger Yankuba Minteh in January after seeing a €60 million bid rejected over the summer. (Sport Witness)

- The Reds have also held talks with Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara, 22, over a move. (Caught Offside)

- Bayern Munich are considering a summer move for Newcastle United striker Nick Woltemade, with the Magpies prepared to listen to permanent offers. (Football Insider)

- Newcastle and Barcelona are in the race to land Norway midfielder Bo Hegland, 22, from Swedish side Djurgårdens IF. (Football Insider)

- Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta intends to block loan offers to sign winger Noni Madueke amid interest from Juventus and Atlético Madrid. (Football Insider)

- England captain Harry Kane is prioritizing his future at Bayern Munich despite ongoing interest and monitoring from Manchester United. (Football Insider)

- Juventus are considering signing a free-agent goalkeeper following an injury to Kamil Grabara, with Neto and Sergio Rico offering themselves to the club. (Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Marseille intervened late in the summer window to prevent winger Igor Paixão from completing a €30 million transfer to Sunderland. (Le Journal du Dimanche)

- Tottenham Hotspur, Aston Villa, Juventus, and AC Milan are tracking the situation of Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-jae. (Ekrem Konur)

stories.headline: Hawks rookie Henri Veesaar (ACL) expected to miss season
stories.summary: Hawks rookie 7-footer Henri Veesaar suffered a torn ACL in his right knee during a workout last week and is expected to miss the season.
stories.body:
Atlanta Hawks rookie center Henri Veesaar is expected to miss the 2026-27 season after tearing the ACL in his right knee.

Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15 and will undergo surgery in October. The 7-foot center was drafted with the 52nd overall pick by the LA Clippers and was traded to Atlanta.

Veesaar, 22, averaged 17 points, 8.7 rebounds, 1.2 blocks and 42.6% 3-point shooting in 31 starts for North Carolina during his senior season.

The Hawks also announced they signed guard Isaac McKneely, who averaged 6.7 points, 1.6 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 18.9 minutes during Atlanta's two summer leagues.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Union skyrocket as unbeaten streak reaches 11 games
stories.summary: Can anyone stop the Philadelphia Union? Their latest win powered them up the charts in this week's edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

In one of the most important matches of their end-of-season schedule, Sam Surridge scored in the fourth and 91st minutes to help secure a 2-2 draw against Miami. With the point, Nashville is winless in three (two draws, one defeat) but still in a position to break Inter's Supporters' Shield record with nine games to go.

2. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 2

Nashville further tightened their grip on the Supporters' Shield with a 3-0 win over Chicago on Saturday. A dominant first-half display mixed with some savvy transition attacking in the second half saw all three of the club's designated players find the back of the net.

3. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 3

The Whitecaps took care of business against Salt Lake by a 3-0 scoreline, thoroughly outplaying their hosts. Few teams in the league can match Vancouver for attacking difference-makers, with summer signing Yadaly Diaby making his first league start and notching two goal contributions.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 4

Inching closer to full health, star left back Sergio Reguilón saw the field in the second half as Miami played to a 2-2 draw with San Diego. While the attack still lacks balance without a threat coming down the wings, even a partially hampered Inter Miami squad still boasts some of the sport's best-ever attackers. Lionel Messi and Luis Suárez both found the back of the net Sunday.

5. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 8

Riding the high of his first call-up to the U.S. men's national team, Peyton Miller bagged a brace in the Revolution's 4-2 victory over Orlando on Saturday. With his sizzling speed and developing goal threat, the 18-year-old did well to help lead New England in the absence of the injured Jack Harrison.

6. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 13

Can anyone stop the Union? Despite falling into a three-goal hole on the road in Kansas City, Philadelphia scored four goals in a nine-minute span in the second half to claim a 4-3 win. They've now gone 11 straight games without a loss in league play.

7. LAFC
Previous ranking: 6

Despite taking a 2-0 lead over San Jose in the California Clásico, a 10-man LAFC couldn't hold on for all three points against their in-state rivals. Two second-half concessions, including one late in stoppage time, turned three points into one in a 2-2 draw.

8. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 11

Allan Saint-Maximin opened his Charlotte account with a goal in a 2-1 victory over D.C. United on Saturday. If coach Dean Smith can tap into the former Newcastle man's one-on-one dribbling and his goal threat, Charlotte FC will be a difficult postseason out.

9. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 10

For more than 45 minutes of action, it looked as if Mateusz Bogusz's penalty conversion had sealed a win for the Dynamo over Cincinnati. However, late in second-half stoppage time, the Polish attacker conceded a penalty that allowed the visitors to equalize at 2-2.

10. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 12

Missing Antoine Griezmann because of a thigh injury suffered in their midweek U.S. Open Cup semifinal defeat, Orlando fell 4-2 to New England. Outside of Lionel Messi, there might not be a player more important to his team's trophy chances than the Frenchman.

11. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 9

A 3-0 loss to Nashville marked seven straight games across all competitions for the Fire without a win. While Robert Lewandowski's scoring record has been positive since he arrived in MLS, it looks as if Chicago's major shift up top has destabilized so much of what propelled them in the spring.

12. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 7

Life has been a slog for New York City lately. A series of poor results over the past two months was extended to include a 1-0 defeat Friday at the hands of their biggest rivals: Red Bull New York. While they created enough chances to win, conversion in front of goal lagged for NYCFC.

13. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 5

Cincinnati left it late but managed to earn a 2-2 road draw against the Dynamo. Kévin Denkey's penalty in the 97th minute rescued the trip, though that doesn't change the fact that Pat Noonan's team has gone five games without a victory.

14. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

After three consecutive victories before this weekend, Dallas played Austin to a 0-0 draw Saturday. Though they created the better chances, Brad Stuver's impressive goalkeeping limited the home side to a solitary point.

15. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 17

It was hardly a dominant showing from the Galaxy, but Greg Vanney's team managed a comeback 3-2 victory on the road in Minnesota, with a makeshift front line that featured Chucky Lozano playing underneath the striker and fullback Harbor Miller back in the attack. Still, all three points count the same.

16. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 16

Thanks to a brace from Anders Dreyer, San Diego earned a 2-2 draw with Miami on Sunday night. While the sophomore outfit still sits below the playoff line out West, they only trail the ninth-placed Portland Timbers by a single point.

17. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 21

Though their summer slide saw San Jose tumble down these rankings, things have stabilized for the Quakes. Their 2-2 draw with LAFC on Saturday marked five straight results, and Timo Werner's return from injury made the outing all the brighter.

18. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 15

Salt Lake were never truly in their match against Vancouver, allowing two goals in the first 30 minutes and failing to ever mount a convincing attack. With Diego Luna now expected to miss the rest of the season with a knee injury, RSL's path to contention is murkier than at any prior point in the season.

19. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 20

Between his call-up to the U.S. men's national team and his goal to cap off a 1-0 win for Red Bull New York in the Hudson River derby against New York City, Julian Hall has had quite the week. Along the way, Michael Bradley's team defended well for much of Friday's game, which hasn't always been true of them in 2026.

20. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 22

The Sounders' summer signings helped rescue a 3-3 draw in Colorado, with Dejan Joveljić and Caden Clark each nabbing a goal to see their new outfit equalize in Colorado. For a team that's still dealing with a slew of injuries, every point is crucial.

21. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 25

Don't look now, but Austin have managed seven straight results in league play. Most recently, they held Dallas to a scoreless draw thanks to some impressive goalkeeping and possession control. It's not flashy, but there's momentum building for 2027.

22. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 27

The good? New winger Morgan Whittaker scored a brace in his first MLS start and looks the part of a superstar. The bad? The Rapids blew a multigoal lead to draw 3-3 at home with Seattle.

23. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 26

Laurent Courtois' return to Montréal went as well as the interim manager could've hoped. His Columbus team dispatched their hosts -- who double as the Frenchman's former employer -- by a 2-0 scoreline.

24. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 18

Minnesota have dropped points from winning or even positions in each of their past five games, including Saturday's 3-2 home loss to the Galaxy. It's safe to say things have gone off the rails for the Loons.

25. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 19

Every now and then, you come up against a team that puts you in your place. That's what happened for Toronto in their 3-1 loss to St. Louis. There's still a distance for Toronto to go before they're on the level of MLS's best.

26. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 24

The Timbers put up a valiant late-game effort and scored in the 93rd minute, but it wasn't enough to salvage a point in Texas as they stumbled to a 2-1 defeat to Dallas.

27. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 23

While they largely outplayed Charlotte, D.C. still fell 2-1. Even when the team plays well, results still aren't trickling into the nation's capital. D.C. United have just six wins this season, one more than bottom-feeders Montréal and Kansas City.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

There haven't been as many moments of Aleksei Miranchuk magic as Atlanta would've hoped for when they signed him from Atalanta, but the playmaker delivered Saturday. His goal made the difference in the Five Stripes' 1-0 road win over the Timbers.

29. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 29

What looked destined to be a second straight impressive victory for Kansas City turned into a disaster when the hosts conceded four goals in less than 10 minutes to Philadelphia to lose 4-3 on Saturday. Still, André Luiz dominating in the attack after joining this summer is a silver lining.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

Up against their old head coach, Courtois, Montréal fell 2-0 at home to the Crew. At least they're through to the Canadian Championship final?

stories.headline: Small changes in biggest weight class in MMA divisional rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
The UFC's heavyweight division appears to be stuck in neutral gear.

It's not just about Tom Aspinall vacating the championship on Monday because he is still recovering from an eye injury suffered in last October's no-contest in a title defense against Ciryl Gane. Gane, who won the interim championship with a knockout of Alex Pereira in June, remains atop the ESPN rankings. The top 10 still features Aspinall -- he's eligible to be ranked until the middle of next month, when he will have been inactive for a year -- and includes two heavyweights from outside the UFC in the top six (Francis Ngannou, Vadim Nemkov).

The heavyweight rankings underwent small changes as a result of Saturday's UFC matchup of top-10 fighters Waldo Cortes Acosta and Curtis Blaydes. Cortes Acosta entered the weekend ranked sixth, but after losing by unanimous decision, he drops to No. 9. Blaydes is one spot above him, moving up from 10th.

The only other movement in the divisional rankings is at women's flyweight, where former UFC champion Alexa Grasso moves up one position to No. 4 after Saturday's unanimous decision win over Manon Fiorot. Formerly ranked second, Fiorot drops three spots after her first loss in a nontitle bout since her pro debut in 2018.

Here are the ESPN pound-for-pound MMA rankings and a list of current UFC champions in all weight classes.

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: NRL investigating after referee peppered with rubbish
stories.summary: Warriors great Shaun Johnson has labelled footage of fans throwing projectiles at referee Ashley Klein in Auckland as embarrassing, with the NRL investigating.
stories.body:
The NRL has been urged to come down hard on supporters who peppered referee Ashley Klein with projectiles as the league's integrity unit investigates the ugly aftermath of Newcastle's semifinal win over the Warriors.

Vision from Eden Park after fulltime in the Knights' 12-10 victory showed Klein being hit with a raft of bottles, cups and rubbish as he walked from the field.

The footage shows Klein having to be protected by security, as fans abused the veteran referee and projectiles rained down on him.

The NRL immediately launched an investigation into potential breaches of their spectators' code of conduct. An Integrity Unit investigator had been at the ground.

"If found guilty, they will be banned for a period of time from attending NRL games," ARL Commission chairman Peter V'landys told AAP.

V'landys' no-nonsense stance was welcomed by the referee's union, Professional Rugby League Match Officials (PRLMO), who called on the NRL to come down hard on the Warriors supporters.

"The safety of all referees and match officials is paramount, and they should be allowed to perform their duties without being placed in harm's way," PRLMO chair John Choueifate told AAP.

"To say I was disappointed is an understatement and call on the NRL to investigate the incident which detracted from an enthralling match.

"They need to send a very clear message to those responsible and to others in future that this rubbish must be stamped out of the game."

New Zealand Police confirmed no arrests were made, with "no issues to note" other than two pitch invaders.

The Warriors did not respond to AAP requests for comment.

Sunday's crowd of 48,511 marked the biggest ever for a rugby league match in New Zealand, after the NRL made the call to move the game from the Warriors' traditional Mt Smart Stadium home.

The NRL's investigation came as they admitted Klein had erred with a crucial decision not to penalise Newcastle prop Tyson Frizell for an escort in the dying minutes.

Had it been awarded, the Warriors could have levelled at 12-12 and sent the game to extra time. It's understood Klein will be dropped for the preliminary finals.

Regardless, Warriors great Shaun Johnson hit out at fans, labelling their behaviour as "embarrassing" and said a missed call was no excuse for that reaction.

"Ashley Klein is a human being in the middle of a park doing one of the toughest jobs there is," Johnson said on his Instagram.

"In what world do we think that is okay? You guys are so quick to point out that athletes and ex-athletes are role models for your kids.

"Well you're not setting the bar very high if that's what they've got to look up to. Be better man.

"It's such a s--- way to finish a season. Not just from a result standpoint. But leaving such a sour taste from a fan base. A fan base I deeply care about."

Warriors coach Andrew Webster had vented his frustration in the postmatch press conference, highlighting a bunker strip call on Te Maire Martin and the decision not to penalise Frizell for a possible escort on Leka Halasima.

The incident comes after AFL umpires also had cans thrown at them while leaving the MCG after Hawthorn's tight loss to Brisbane in Saturday night's preliminary final.

The AFL has also condemned the behaviour and warned of minimum five-year bans for any fans found responsible.

stories.headline: Atlanta Dream beat the New York Liberty 95-84, close in on a top-4 WNBA seed
stories.summary: — Jordin Canada scored 19 points, Angel Reese added 18 points and 10 rebounds, and the Atlanta Dream beat the New York Liberty 95-84 on Monday night.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- — Jordin Canada scored 19 points, Angel Reese added 18 points and 10 rebounds, and the Atlanta Dream beat the New York Liberty 95-84 on Monday night.


DeWanna Bonner had 17 points and Rhyne Howard 16 for the Dream (29-14), who moved closer to clinching a top-four seed in the WNBA playoffs. A win against New York on Wednesday or a loss by Indiana in one of its final two games would give the Dream home court in the opening round of the postseason.


The Liberty (26-17) had their three-game winning streak end and now will be on the road in the opening round of the playoffs.


Atlanta led by three at the half and extended the lead to 73-62 after three quarters thanks to Allisha Gray and Howard. After a scoreless first half, Gray had 12 points in the period, including seven during a 9-2 run to start it. Howard then took over with 10 points in the quarter.


New York, which played in Toronto on Sunday, got within eight a few times, but could get no closer.


Breanna Stewart had 27 points and 14 rebounds to lead the Liberty. Jonquel Jones added 18 points and 12 rebounds.


New York was up by one after the first quarter as Pauline Astier had 10 points. The Liberty held Howard and Gray in check as they missed all five of their shots in the opening period.


It stayed tight in the second quarter with neither team able to get much separation. Bonner grabbed an offensive rebound with 3.1 seconds left and was fouled as she converted the basket. Her three-point play gave the Dream a 41-38 lead at the half. The Liberty were 1 for 13 from behind the 3-point arc in the first half.


The Liberty honored all seven of their women's FIBA World Cup participants before the game. The team had at least one player on all four of the semifinal teams and Stewart led the U.S. to the gold medal and earned MVP honors of the tournament. Marine Johannes and Astier were on France, which took home the silver medal. Raquel Carrera was on Spain, which won the bronze.

stories.headline: 2026 NBA buzz: Latest free agency and trade updates
stories.summary: We're tracking deals, trades and buzz across the NBA, including Pelle Larsson getting a long-term extension with the Heat.
stories.body:
NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 21

Charania: Pistons, Duren at an "impasse"
Free agent center Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons are at an impasse this season and the franchise is uncertain if he will show up to next Monday's Media Day, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

"When you talk to people close to [Duren], he feels a certain way toward the Pistons' respect level for him," Charania said on NBA Today. "For him it's been all about respect, for the team it has just been about business. ... Over the course of this offseason, his offer has been been around the $180 to $190 million over five years range. And that has also included incentives like weight clauses to my understanding. And that has all played a part in this as well.

"Over the last several weeks it's kind of quiet on this front. The sides have picked up communication. And I am told right now the Pistons offer to Jalen Duren is $200 million over five years."

Duren has until Oct. 1 to sign a qualifying offer.

Hawks' Henri Veesaar out with torn ACL

The Atlanta Hawks announced that center Henri Veesaar tore his ACL during a Sept. 15 workout. He will undergo surgery in October and is expected to miss the entire 2026-27 season.

Sept. 18

Pistons, Thompson reach five-year, $155 million extension
Detroit Pistons All-Defensive forward Ausar Thompson has agreed to a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN.

Thompson lands the fully guaranteed extension after making first-team All-Defense and finishing third in Defensive Player of the Year voting last season. The 23-year-old averaged 9.9 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 0.9 blocks in 2025-26 while leading the NBA in steals per game (2.0).

Heat, Larsson agree to four-year, $60 million extension
Miami Heat guard Pelle Larsson has agreed to a new four-year, $60 million contract extension, with a mutual option for the 2030-31 season, Austin Brown and Steven Heumann of CAA Sports told ESPN on Friday.

A second-round find in the 2024 draft, the 6-foot-5 guard avoids restricted free agency next summer and locks in a new deal with a mutual option that fully guarantees $60 million while allowing either side to opt in on 2030.

Jazz, George agree on a five-year, rookie-scale extension
Utah Jazz guard Keyonte George have agreed on a five-year, $157.5 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania and Tim MacMahon. George was the No. 16 pick in the 2023 draft and has averaged 17.2 points and 5.3 assists per game in his three seasons with the Jazz.

Sept. 17

Bey, Pelicans agree to three-year extension
New Orleans Pelicans' Saddiq Bey agreed to a three-year, $55.5 million contract extension with the franchise, plus a trade kicker, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Bey averaged a career-high 17.7 points per game last season after missing all of the 2024-25 season with a torn ACL.

Sept. 16

Kings remain interested in Duren
The Sacramento Kings continue to loom in the background of Jalen Duren's restricted free agency with the incumbent Detroit Pistons.

Kings general manager Scott Perry met with Duren for dinner in Miami in early July and has maintained a level of steady interest in the ultimate outcome of Duren's free agency, though a path to acquire Duren this summer remains blocked.

The Pistons declined any legitimate conversation about a Duren sign-and-trade to the Kings for starting center Domantas Sabonis and have maintained a strong stance about their intention to keep Duren.

As ESPN reported earlier this month, the Pistons have a five-year offer in the $35 million per year range on the table, but that hasn't been enough to entice the disgruntled Duren to sign.

His greatest piece of leverage is a risky one -- the $9.6 million qualifying offer that would make him an unrestricted free agent next summer, when Sacramento will have flexibility for the first time in Perry's tenure as general manager. Zach LaVine's $48.9 million contract and De'Andre Hunter's $24.9 million contract both expire, allowing the Kings to generate a max offer for Duren, should he be available.

But that would only be the case if Duren is willing to take a massive one-year paycut and accept the risk of the qualifying offer. Until then, the Kings remain in the background as an interested long-term suitor helping Duren's leverage. -- Anthony Slater

Knicks sign Brown to training camp contract
The New York Knicks are signing Bruce Brown to a training camp contract, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. New York will also have "John Konchar, Drew Eubanks and others enter camp to compete for the final regular season roster," per Charania.

Sept. 15

Shams: NBA Las Vegas expansion plans due Thursday
The NBA and commissioner Adam Silver are in deep expansion conversations with Las Vegas, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania, with the next round of bids due Thursday. Charania also reported that the final round of bids will be due shortly after this round and that his understanding is that the Las Vegas expansion proposal could exceed $10 billion.

Why Dolan is so worried about the second apron
The New York Knicks' championship parade has not even started, but there are already questions over whether finances will break up the roster.

"If we could bring back the whole team, exactly as is, why wouldn't you?" Knicks owner James Dolan said Wednesday on WFAN's "Carton Show." "I don't know if we'll be able to.

"We're willing to stretch, but there's certain things in the NBA that you'd have to be suicidal to do. One of them is the second apron. Cannot go into the second apron."

Including the 24th pick in next week's draft (June 23 and 24, 8 p.m. ET on ABC/ESPN), New York is $13 million below the second apron and has decisions with free agents Landry Shamet, Mitchell Robinson and possibly Jose Alvarado. (Alvarado has until Monday to decide on his $4.5 million option.) The entire starting five, meanwhile, is under contract through at least 2026-27. Karl-Anthony Towns is extension-eligible this summer and can become a free agent in the 2027 offseason if an agreement is not reached.

The second apron is a punitive luxury tax threshold restricting how teams add to their rosters in free agency, trades and the draft. In the case of the Knicks, the team would not be allowed to send cash in a trade, use the $6.1 million tax midlevel exception, aggregate salaries in a trade or use more than 100% of the traded player exception.

A team cannot trade its first-round pick seven years out if it finishes over the second apron in consecutive seasons, which no team has ever done. That same pick could be moved back to the end of the first round if a team finishes over the second apron in three out of four seasons. Luckily for Dolan and the Knicks, there are no rules that prohibit a team from retaining its own players.

New York can exceed the threshold to sign Robinson, Shamet and Alvarado. If the Knicks let the three players sign elsewhere, they would have their first-round pick (New York also has the 31st and 55th picks in the second round), the $6.1 million tax midlevel exception and $2.5 million veteran minimum exceptions available as replacements.

Since the apron rules were implemented before the 2024-25 season, Cleveland, Phoenix, Minnesota and Boston have finished the regular season over the second apron. The Knicks finished the past two seasons $53,000 and $370,000 below. Next offseason, New York is projected to be $31 million below the second apron with seven players under contract. -- Bobby Marks

Even though Chicago sits 29-49 and in 12th place in the Eastern Conference, the opening is expected to be an attractive one around the league. The Bulls have flexibility on how they can build their roster with their own lottery pick, approximately $60 million in cap space and young players on the roster without long-term salary commitments.

Chicago is still expected to try to retain coach Billy Donovan in some capacity after the season. -- Jamal Collier

Bulls fire Karnisovas, Eversley

The fractured relationship between Giannis and the Milwaukee Bucks
ESPN's Shams Charania went inside the drama between two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Milwaukee Bucks, as a crucial summer window approaches. The story details what has led to the falling out in Milwaukee and what it means for the future of both Antetokounmpo and the Bucks.

This season, the Bucks have gone 17-19 with Antetokounmpo in the lineup and 14-28 without him, and they rank 25th in offensive rating and 26th in defensive rating overall. They are one of six NBA teams to rank in the bottom five in both categories.
All the while, the uncertainty of Antetokounmpo's future in Milwaukee lingered. The Bucks engaged in trade talks ahead of the Feb. 5 trade deadline but chose to hold on to him, even as it became increasingly clear that they didn't have much hope of even elevating into the play-in race. Milwaukee is now headed to the draft lottery for the first time since 2016, snapping a streak of nine consecutive years in the playoffs. The Bucks haven't won a postseason series since 2022. Antetokounmpo, who is under contract for one more season, has played in a career-low 36 games and privately feuded with the organization for several months, culminating in rebuking the team's requests to shut down in the final month of the season and setting up another contentious summer.

"When your best player is one foot in, one foot out," said one team source, "you're not going to win."

The Bucks have officially been eliminated from the playoffs.

Inside the Bucks' lost season

Bulls part ways with front office leaders, Karnisovas and Eversley

Williamson unlocks more money in 61st game
New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson has reached another financial benchmark for games played.

The salary protection for his $42.2 million salary in 2026-27 was nonguaranteed headed into the season. But now that he has played in 61 games, 80% ($33.7 million) of his $42.2 million salary for next season is protected.

The remaining $8.4 million will become guaranteed if Williamson's combined body weight and body fat percentage is less than 295. There were seven times he was required to weigh in this season. It's unclear what he weighed during those check-ins.

Williamson has one of the league's most unusual contracts. His salary next season and in 2027-28 originally became nonguaranteed when he missed more than 22 games in the 2022-23 season. His $44.9 million salary in 2027-28 remains nonguaranteed.

The 61 games played this season is tied for the third most in his career. He's averaging 21.1 points and 5.7 rebounds per game. The Pelicans, who have been eliminated from playoff contention, have four games left on their schedule. -- Bobby Marks

Doncic out for the rest of the regular season
Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic is out indefinitely with a Grade 2 right hamstring injury, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania and Dave McMenamin. Doncic will miss the rest of the regular season, and his availability for the playoffs is uncertain.

In the 20 minutes after the news broke, the Lakers' title chances dropped from 30-1 to 100-1, per DraftKings Sportsbook.

Doncic, who has played in 64 games and ranked fourth in ESPN's latest MVP straw poll, will apply for what's called an "extraordinary circumstances challenge" to the 65-game rule for award consideration, per his agent, Bill Duffy.

Per ESPN's Bobby Marks, Doncic can apply the exception for the two games he missed in December for the birth of his daughter. The application must be made no earlier than 12 p.m. ET on the last day of the regular season and no later than 11:59 p.m. on the day after the last day of the regular season.

Doncic signed a three-year extension last August and has been named All-NBA in five of the six previous seasons.

There will be no financial implications in his next contract if the application is denied.

Though the Lakers haven't provided a timeline for his return, Grade 2 hamstring injuries typically require a monthlong recovery. Doncic has averaged a league-high 33.5 points this season, along with 7.7 rebounds and 8.3 assists.

The Lakers, who have gone 8-2 in their past 10 games, are third in the Western Conference, one game ahead of the No. 4-seeded Denver Nuggets, 2.5 games ahead of the No. 5-seeded Houston Rockets and 3.5 ahead of the No. 6-seeded Minnesota Timberwolves.

stories.headline: Dreyer outduels Messi as San Diego hands Miami 4th straight draw
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored his 101st goal for Inter Miami CF, but Anders Dreyer scored twice for San Diego FC, as the teams played to a 2-2 draw on Sunday night.
stories.body:
MIAMI -- Lionel Messi scored his 101st goal for Inter Miami CF, but Anders Dreyer scored twice for San Diego FC, as the teams played to a 2-2 draw on Sunday night.

It was Inter Miami's fourth consecutive draw in MLS play as new manager Kily González oversaw his first league game in charge of the club and cut a frustrated figure after conceding a late goal to drop points.

"We've been here for four days and haven't been able to train properly. Defensively, we really need to be much stronger," González said after the game. "We can't commit these defensive horrors, they come at a high cost. That final situation shouldn't have happened. It's surreal to be in a position to win the game, yet nearly lose it.

"We only avoided defeat because our goalkeeper saved us."

Dreyer gave San Diego a 1-0 lead in the 12th minute, capitalizing on a through ball from Jeppe Tverskov before deftly chipping over goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair.

Messi answered in the 24th with his 20th league goal of the season. His free kick from the right side went untouched through the penalty area and into the far side of the net, four days after he scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in a 2-0 win over Mexican side Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup.

"I think the Campeones Cup might have had an unconscious effect, especially in the first half, leading to a bit of complacency," González added. "These are factors that are part of football. At a club where we are obliged to win every match we play, we have to rise to the occasion. We made significant adjustments at halftime to get the team flowing and ensure we stayed compact, keeping the lines tight so we wouldn't suffer the way we did in the first half."

The goal was Messi's eighth from a free kick since entering the league in 2023, more than any other player in MLS during that time span.

Luis Suárez put Miami ahead in the 74th minute as Miami looked set to leapfrog New England into second place in the Eastern Conference, but Dreyer scored his second of the night eight minutes later with another fine finish -- this time from a ball over the top of the Herons' backline.

Miami is now in third place with a record of 12-4-10 with 46 points -- 11 behind first-place Nashville.

"But anyway, we have to keep going," González said. "On the positive side, we did some good things, but I need to fine-tune the defensive side because that's what really worries me most."

Earlier Sunday, FIFA announced that the final phase of the 2027 FIFA Women's Champions Cup will be played at Inter Miami's home of Nu Stadium in January. FIFA Chief Football Officer Jill Ellis spoke at halftime about bringing the competition to Miami.

"I think we've seen that this city loves its football. We've seen it this past summer with the World Cup," Ellis said. "I think it's time to bring a major women's tournament here to Miami. I think it's exciting."

Miami returns to MLS play next Sunday on the road against the Columbus Crew, while San Diego is also on the road with a game against Austin FC on Saturday.

ESPN writer Lizzy Becherano contributed to this report, while information from The Associated Press was also used.

stories.headline: UFC 331 takeaways: Are we living in the greatest era for lightweights?
stories.summary: Arman Tsarukyan and Joshua Van stole the show with emphatic statements at UFC 331.
stories.body:
The main card of UFC 331 had shocking moments on top of shocking moments on top of pound-for-pound resume building.

First, Sean Sharaf got his first UFC win as the biggest underdog in the promotion's history against Olympic gold medalist Gable Steveson in just 12 seconds. Then Arman Tsarukyan stepped into the cage for the first time this year and reminded everyone why the current crop of UFC lightweights may be the best ever. And flyweight champion Joshua Van followed it all up with a performance that should place him among the 10 best MMA fighters in the world right now. What more could an MMA fan want?

Van is a top five pound-for-pound fighter
I can't believe I'm saying this -- not because Van isn't great or hasn't been great for some time. It's just -- how does one become a top-five fighter in the world at age 24, with less than five years of pro experience?

After his performance on Saturday, I can't talk about Van anymore as just a phenom or a young champion. He is legitimately as good as just about anyone in the entire sport. Alexandre Pantoja coming off injury looked like the same Pantoja as before the injury. If anything, he looked even more determined than before. His pressure was appropriate and his decision-making was sound. Van was just better.

He defended takedowns and escaped on the ground when Pantoja could get him there. At one point, was it just me or did Van catch Pantoja's glove as he threw a punch, before countering? He caught some of Pantoja's kicks, in the same way he caught the one in December that led to Pantoja's injury. In the fifth round, when the result of the fight still felt up in the air, Van delivered his best five minutes of work, dropping Pantoja with a right hand.

Van is gifted athletically, confident and a natural finisher. He's been all of that from the first moment we saw him. One description that shouldn't be forgotten, however, is that he's extremely technical. This was one of the most technical fights of the entire year, against one of the best flyweights of all time, and Van ended up running away on the scorecards. If Van were 28, I don't think anyone would have an issue ranking him near the top of the pound-for-pound. The only hesitancy to do it is because -- it doesn't seem right or possible, given his age and relative inexperience. I'm getting over that. Van is top five. -- Brett Okamoto

Are we living in the greatest lightweight era of all time?

The history of the UFC's lightweight division is so undeniably rich. One of the division's greatest "eras" was from 2016 to 2020, when Conor McGregor became double champ at Madison Square Garden, Khabib Nurmagomedov dominated and timeless fighters such as Tony Ferguson, Dustin Poirier and Justin Gaethje were in their primes.

This upcoming chapter at lightweight has a chance to challenge all that.

Within the past three months, Ilia Topuria has suffered his first loss (in spectacular fashion to Gaethje on the White House lawn) and vowed revenge. Paddy Pimblett has turned in a star-making performance, submitting Benoît Saint Denis in less than a minute on a McGregor-headlined card. And now Arman Tsarukyan has completed an unbelievable walkoff knockout of Mauricio Ruffy. Topuria, Pimblett and Tsarukyan are three legitimate superstar storylines, and it just so happens they are all rivals who have promised to take each other out.

Don't forget that the champion, Gaethje, could postpone retirement in order to defend his throne. Veterans Max Holloway and Charles Oliveira are still active in the top five, too. Australia's Quillan Salkilld has had a breakout year, and Nurmagomedov's younger cousin, Usman, could potentially transition to the UFC after years of dominance in the PFL.

Yeah. The next few years could be the best in lightweight history, and that is really, really saying something. -- Okamoto

The Steveson train has hit an early crossroads

It's not like Steveson had never lost before. On his way to becoming a 2020 Olympic wrestling gold medalist and two-time NCAA Division I national champion, he was formidable but not perfect. His record at the University of Minnesota was 103-3. His international freestyle record, including cadet and junior levels, was 53-2. Even an all-time great has had to pick himself up and dust himself off at times.

But this defeat was different from whatever Steveson had ever experienced. He got knocked out cold in 12 seconds by Sharaf, a guy who came into their fight 0-2 in the UFC with both losses coming by knockout. Let's just acknowledge that this matchmaking was a setup to build an MMA résumé for Steveson. Considering that he had just four pro fights under his belt, though, this was an appropriate booking.

The result was a shocker. It was the largest known upset in UFC history, per DraftKings. But what's done is done, and the story now takes an unexpected twist. Will this be just a speed bump on Steveson's express road toward the top of the UFC heavyweight division? Or will this defeat make Steveson timid in standup fighting, slowing his development beyond being a one-dimensional wrestler? Heavy-handed UFC heavyweights will surely be emboldened by seeing Steveson crash to the canvas.

What seemed like a sure thing now is surrounded by question marks. The future might still be bright for Steveson. It probably will be. But here's a suggestion for Steveson: Don't bother watching the 12-second KO loss. Why put yourself through that again? Instead, go find video of Islam Makhachev's 2015 KO loss in his second UFC fight, then contemplate how Makhachev has managed to win all 17 of his fights since on his way to becoming the best pound-for-pound fighter in the sport. -- Jeff Wagenheim

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: Klein faces axe as NRL admit crucial refereeing error
stories.summary: The NRL is set to axe top referee Ashley Klein for the preliminary finals after admitting the Warriors were wrongly denied a crucial late penalty in their 12-10 semifinal loss to Newcastle.
stories.body:
The NRL is set to axe top referee Ashley Klein for the preliminary finals after admitting the Warriors were wrongly denied a crucial late penalty in their 12-10 semifinal loss to Newcastle.

NRL officials confirmed on Monday the Warriors should have been awarded a penalty with a minute left in Sunday's Eden Park thriller, for an escort infringement by the Knight's Tyson Frizell.

Had the penalty been awarded, the Warriors would have had the chance to level the scores at 12-12 via a penalty goal from just to the side of the posts and send the match to extra time.

But the call was instead missed on the field, with the bunker unable to review the play despite a stoppage for an injury soon afterwards.

A comprehensive NRL review of Newcastle's 12-10 semifinal did, however, back the bunker over two other contentious calls.

First, it was deemed that bunker official Chris Butler was right to rule Warriors centre Ali Leiataua got a thumb to a ball before it went to ground late in the match.

The NRL also supported the bunker's decision to stick with the on-field call of a strip against Warrior Te Maire Martin.

But it is the non-call on Frizell that will annoy the Warriors more.

The Newcastle veteran appeared to get in the way of Leka Halasima as he chased through on a kick in the Warriors' last attacking raid of the match.

Given the seconds that would have come off the clock while the Warriors lined up the shot, there would likely not have been time for a restart.

"I thought they were trying to find ways to take it off us," Warriors coach Andrew Webster said after the game.

"The last one, two points would have drawn the game, he is going across Leka, pretending to try and catch the ball which they've told us you can't do."

AAP understands Klein will pay for the error by losing his spot in the preliminary finals, with Grant Atkins or Gerard Sutton likely to be called up.

Klein has overseen every game of the past five State of Origin series and two of the last four Grand Finals.

He had been expected to referee last year's decider, before losing out to Atkins following 18 penalties in a Melbourne-Cronulla preliminary final.

Meanwhile, the NRL have threatened bans for fans who threw projectiles at Klein as he walked off Eden Park on Sunday night.

Vision showed a mass of bottles and rubbish being thrown at the long-time official, with Warriors great Shaun Johnson labelling the fans' behaviour "embarrassing".

stories.headline: Pete Alonso homers twice to reach 40 on the season, helps Orioles rally to 4-3 win over Blue Jays
stories.summary: — Pete Alonso homered twice, including a two-run shot in the eighth inning that lifted the Baltimore Orioles to a 4-3 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays on Monday night.
stories.body:
BALTIMORE -- — Pete Alonso homered twice, including a two-run shot in the eighth inning that lifted the Baltimore Orioles to a 4-3 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays on Monday night.


The Orioles are on the verge of elimination in the American League wild-card race, but Alonso has been terrific in his first season with the team. He has 40 home runs — the fourth time he's reached that mark in a season — and he's opened a nine-RBI lead on Triple Crown hopeful Yordan Alvarez of Houston.


In fact, Alonso might be the one who ends up leading the AL in homers and RBI. He's one home run behind Tampa Bay slugger Junior Caminero.


The Blue Jays brought in submarine right-hander Tyler Rogers (2-3) to face Alonso, who became just the second right-handed hitter to homer off him over the last two seasons.


Yennier Cano (4-3) won in relief for the Orioles, and Rico Garcia worked a perfect ninth for his 10th save.


Nathan Lukes and George Springer hit RBI singles during Toronto's three-run first inning, but the Blue Jays fell 3 1/2 games behind the idle Chicago White Sox for the final wild card in the AL.


Trey Yesavage returned to the mound for the Blue Jays after knee inflammation sent him to the injured list in early August. He pitched only two innings, allowing a home run to Alonso in the first.


Gunnar Henderson homered in the sixth for the Orioles and finished a double shy of the cycle.


After the start was delayed 47 minutes because of rain, the first four Toronto batters reached base. Shane Baz was called for a pitch-clock violation with the count full to Brett Bateman. Then he issued another walk to Alejandro Kirk on a debatable checked-swing call.


Lukes and Springer followed with hits to make it 2-0. A sacrifice fly by Sean Keys brought home another run.


Baz held Toronto scoreless after that and made it through 6 2/3 innings.


Bateman left the game with a hip injury after making a sliding catch in center field in the second. X-rays were negative.


Up next
Blue Jays RHP Max Scherzer (3-8) starts Tuesday night against Chris Bassitt (8-5) of the Orioles.
